children: For a central bank that avoids forward guidance at all costs, the Reserve Bank of Australia has done some remarkable work in the last month preparing financial markets for a potential interest rate increase next week. Importantly, the torrent of comments by senior RBA staff might also be aimed at winning votes around the board table. In the spirit of open board debate, RBA Governor Michele Bullock says she's just "one vote." Non-executive board member Iain Ross said this week there is no evidence of a wage-price spiral. His dovishness might imply a split vote is possible next week. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
